name: Full-Horizon Thicket Equality Is the Maximum-Class Equality
statement: If $H\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$, $|X|=n$, and $\operatorname{Ldim}(H)\le d$, then $H$ is $(n,d)$-thicket-maximum exactly when $|H|=\sum_{i=0}^d\binom{n}{i}$; in this case $H$ is a maximum class and $\operatorname{Ldim}(H)=d$.
proof: Querying every coordinate in a fixed order distinguishes all concepts, so $\rho_H(n)=|H|$. Equality with the thicket Sauer bound is therefore exactly the ordinary Sauer cardinality equality. The sequential comparison theorem then forces Littlestone dimension $d$.
